detect.auth_fix_hint: sign in per OpenCode docs, then verify with 'opencode models' (must return a non-empty list)

read-only.native: OPENCODE_CONFIG=<per-handle opencode.json>: permission.edit=deny,bash=deny,webfetch=deny (reads still allowed — OpenCode's read tool is not permission-gated)

dangerous.native: --auto (auto-approves any non-denied permission) + OPENCODE_CONFIG permission.edit=allow,bash=allow,webfetch=allow (written regardless, inert once --auto is passed — mirrors agy's --dangerously-skip-permissions pattern)

notes.posture_caveats: P-OC2b (live probe, real opencode 1.18.5, free model opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free, 2026-07-24, ~20s, bounded by a 90s perl-alarm — never hung): a write attempt under read-only (permission:{edit:deny,bash:deny,webfetch:deny}) auto-denies at the TOOL-AVAILABILITY level, not via an interactive approval prompt — the model's own 'Available tools' list simply excludes write/edit/bash entirely ('Model tried to call unavailable tool bash. Available tools: glob, grep, invalid, read, skill, task, todowrite, websearch'), it retries once via a sub-task, and then explains in plain text that it cannot write and suggests the caller run the shell command themselves. No file was created (config genuinely held). IMPORTANT for cmd_status's generic (non-agy) NO_OUTPUT path: unlike agy's silent-empty-stdout denial, opencode's denied-write turns usually end with a NON-EMPTY explanatory text answer — is_blank_file will be false and the turn reports a normal SUCCESS with that explanation as the answer, not NO_OUTPUT. adapter_permission_hint_pattern still covers the narrower case where a denied turn ends with no text part at all.
notes.id_capture: every --format json event line carries a top-level "sessionID":"ses_..." field; adapter_capture_session_id slurps turn-1's events.jsonl and takes the first value matching ^ses_[A-Za-z0-9]+$ (typed JSON select, never a raw string grep over untrusted model output)
notes.binary_location: real opencode installs to ~/.opencode/bin/opencode and is NOT on the non-interactive Bash PATH — adapter_detect/opencode_resolve_bin check PATH, then ~/.opencode/bin, then an OPENCODE_BIN override, in that order
notes.answer_extraction: opencode has no native -o/--output-last-message flag; the per-turn helper script this adapter writes under $DIR (turn-NNN.run.sh) runs opencode with its stdout inherited to the engine's eventsfile (same fd the turn-supervisor.pl child already redirects, so events.jsonl needs no separate copy step), then re-reads that same file with jq to extract the final {"type":"text",...,"part":{"type":"text","text":...}} event(s) into turn-NNN.last-message.txt BEFORE exiting — required because extdel.sh's cmd_status routes any cli other than "agy" through its generic (codex-shaped) branch, which expects last-message.txt to already be populated by the time the turn is terminal and does not itself copy from events.jsonl the way the agy-specific branch does.
notes.known_engine_limitation: validate_handle() in extdel.sh (line ~190) hardcodes the handle grammar to literal ^(codex|agy)-... rather than a generic ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*-... — this predates the opencode adapter and is NOT fixed here (out of scope: zero edits to extdel.sh). Effect: 'start --cli opencode' works fully (cmd_start never calls validate_handle on its own freshly-minted handle), and the turn genuinely runs to completion under the real supervisor/mock, but 'status'/'prompt'/'slice'/'stop' against an opencode-* handle are rejected with a generic 'no such handle' ERROR by every caller going through extdel.sh's CLI surface, even though the handle directory demonstrably exists. See tests/test-extdel-opencode-resume.sh section 0 for a reproduction and plugins/sdlc-simple-orchestration/scripts/extdel.sh:190.
